What one value of a plan's time column stands for

Source: R/time.R
time_basis_levels.Rd

A plan's @time_basis. "day", "week" and "month" are Date columns holding the first day of the period, so a row covers that day, that week, or that calendar month. "instant" is a POSIXct column holding the exact moment a buy runs — a dated spot, an 8pm takeover, a half-hour sponsorship.

Usage

time_basis_levels()

Value

A character vector of the valid, canonical values.

Details

A timed row is keyed by the moment it starts, and its length is its flight's: a 30-second spot flighted 20:00:00 to 20:00:30 covers half a minute, a sponsorship flighted 20:00 to 20:30 covers half an hour, and a moment with no flight is a point in time. That is the same rule as every other basis — the row's period, resolved against the buy it belongs to — with the difference that a timed buy occupies exactly one row, so there is nothing to spread across.

The basis is tied to the column's type: a Date column is "day", "week" or "month", and a POSIXct column is always "instant".

See also

media_plan_from_df(), period_basis_levels() for the flight cadence, which is a different thing: what kind of buy a flight is, rather than what one plan row covers.

Examples

time_basis_levels()
#> [1] "day"     "week"    "month"   "instant"
